paras: STINKY BINKIE BABY STEVIE
~A Kids Book~
by: Jeff Rivera
Dedicated to my nephew Job

“Ew! No way!” Venie screamed. “Venie Leenie Barbie Greenlee, you asked for more responsibility. So, get at it!” her mommy exclaimed. “But … baby diapers are so gross!” Venie pouted. The smell coming from her little baby brother’s diaper was the last thing she wanted to smell. Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie was cute with his munchkin cheeks, curly hair and long eyelashes but he sure did stink. “That’s part of being a big sister. Now, do what you’re told,” her mommy said. She set down the baby powder, baby wipes and oh-so-fresh new diaper. “Do I have to?” Venie asked. “Do you want to spend the night at Falisha’s?” her mom said. Venie definitely wanted to spend the night at Falisha’s. She always had gumballs and lollipops and sweet buttered popcorn, her favorites. Besides, Falisha was her best friend and always had the best stories, like the time she went down the toilet to rescue her brother.  Venie wasn’t sure she believed her, but it was still a good story. “Well, okay…” Venie groaned. “Now, listen,” her mommy said. “You stay upstairs and watch Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie while I go downstairs and take a nap.” “All by myself?” she asked. “You can do it,” her mom answered. “I trust you.”

And with that, her mom gave her a wink and stepped downstairs. Venie sighed.  “Well, a girl’s gotta do what a girl’s gotta do!” she said as she stepped toward her baby brother. She listened. She could hear her mom snoring like a lawnmower downstairs. Venie didn’t like naps but a nap sounded better than having to change Stinky Binkie’s dirty diaper all by herself. “Goo-goo, ga-ga!” he exclaimed. But before she could get any closer, it happened. First, it sounded like a little whisper, just a Pfft sound. Then, it got even sloppier, messier and louder. Pppppppp! The sound echoed from his diaper and she knew it could only be one thing. “Ew!!!!!” she said, plugging her nose. “You have got to be kidding, Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie! There is no way on God’s green earth I’m going to change your diaper now.” “Goo-goo, ga-ga?” her brother said. “No way!” she repeated. “Sorry, you’re on your own. You’ll just have to change your diaper yourself.”

And with that, she plopped herself on the couch, folded her arms and turned on the TV. It was Saturday morning and she knew it was almost time for her favorite cartoon The Afro Puff Girls. Anything was better than changing Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie’s diaper. “Yay! Cartoons!” Venie said, jumping up and down and leaning toward the TV. “Goo-goo, ga-ga?” her baby brother repeated. “No!” Venie declared. “Goo-goo, ga-ga, ga-ga!” her brother pouted, kicking his feet. “I can’t hear you!” she said, covering her ears and yelling at the top of her lungs. She even turned up the volume. But then, Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie started sniffling, then whimpling, then criffling, then niffling! “Waaaaaaaaaaah!!!!” he screamed at the top of his lungs. She tried to turn the TV up louder to cover up the noise. She pinched her nose to mask the smell. But nothing worked.

“Fine,” she said, turning the TV off. “You ruin everything.” She wondered if it was her imagination but it seemed as if Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie’s diaper had gotten just a little bit bigger. “Ugh!” she said. She held her breath. The smell was just too strong. “You smell like a hundred billion skunks smooshed together in a rotten sandwich,” she told him. “Ga-ga?” he said. “Yes, you do,” she said. As she got closer, the waves of stinkiness attacked her nose like a million red ants.  Venie just knew she couldn’t go through with it -- no way, no how. There was only one solution. She picked her baby brother up, held him at arm's length and walked him right down the hall and into his nursery. “Sorry, Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie but you’re just too stinky for me!” she said. She set him in his crib and opened up the window. “Goodness!” she said. She breathed in the fresh air but even that wasn’t enough. “I can’t take it anymore! You’re just too stinky!” She ran to the door as quickly as she could. “See ya! Wouldn’t wanna be ya!” She let out her breath and clutched her chest. “Finally, now I can watch Afro Puff Girls in peace!”

Back in the nursery, Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie whimpered, his little lips shaking and quivering and livering. A tiny tear leaked from his eye as he sat in his gooshy diaper. His nose flexed up and down. “Ga-ga,” he said with a frown. Even he didn’t like the smell. He looked around the room. There were toys everywhere and a balloon floated in the corner. There was even a little musical mobile that played his favorite baby song. But nothing, absolutely nothing could take his mind off the fact that he was just too stinky!

A little bird floated out his window, then landed on the windowsill. “Chirp chirp!” the bird said. Then it got a whiff of Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie’s dirty diaper and fainted right out the window. “Goo-goo?” Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie said. Where did the bird go? he wondered. There was only one thing he could think of doing, and that was to climb out of the crib and look for the bird himself. He grabbed hold of the crib bars and pulled and tugged, tugged and pulled.  He jumped and leaped, leaped and jumped until finally, he had an idea. He reached right into his diaper, bigger than ever now, and smeared some of the gooshiest parts on the crib bars and slid his way right through them. “Ga-ga?” he said, landing safely on the floor. He crawled his way over to the window, up the toy box and right to the windowsill. Where was that bird? he wondered. Only one way to find out, he thought. He climbed right out the window and onto a tree branch.

Try as she may, Venie just couldn’t concentrate on her favorite cartoon. It was a really good episode, too. It was the one where the Afro Puff Girls used their puffing power to stop the Nappies. But no matter what, she just couldn’t stop thinking about her little brother. Yes, he was stinky. Stinkier than ever. Stinkier than four hundred garbage bags. Stinkier than a building size block of Limburger cheese. But she still loved him, even if filling up a diaper was his favorite thing in the world to do. She turned the TV off. Her mom had asked her to take care of Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie. She hopped off the couch and grabbed all the diaper stuff. She stomped her way down the hall and put her hand on the doorknob. “Might as well get it over with!” she said. But Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie was gone. “Where did he go?” she asked herself. It still smelled like he was in the nursery. She looked in the crib. He wasn’t there. She looked in the closet. Nope, not there. She even looked in the toy box. Nope! “Where are you, Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie?!” she screamed at the top of her lungs.

Where was he? That was a good question. Even Stinky Binkie didn’t know. But he did know that he was having the time of his life crawling across the electrical lines.  He’d found the bird but every time he got close to it, it flew away. He couldn’t have smelled that bad. Could he? Either way, he followed it.

Across the electrical poles, and up a mountain, down a forest and even up a skyscraper! He didn’t know where he was. He just kept crawling. There was only one thing that he was sure of. His diaper kept getting bigger. Bigger than a bag, bigger than a dad, bigger than his mouth, bigger than a couch, bigger than a cane, bigger than a plane! His diaper just kept getting bigger and bigger! And people watched from below. They pointed and said, “Who is that baby?” And, “Ugh! Why does it stink so bad!?”

Back at the house, Venie panicked. She’d looked everywhere for Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie and she just couldn’t figure out where he was. She knew she needed help but she couldn’t call her mom. She needed her best friend, Falisha. So, she picked up the phone and dialed. “You did what?” Falisha asked Venie. “You heard me,” Venie said. “And now I don’t know where he is.” “Well, you have to do something,” Falisha said. “Tell your mom.” “No way! She’s downstairs taking a nap and I’ll only get in trouble,” Venie groaned. “Well, then call the president!” Falisha said. “The president?” Venie asked. “Of course. He can solve anything.” Falisha told her. “I think you’re out of your mind,” Venie said. But she couldn’t think of a better idea.

She turned on the TV and that was when she saw it. Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie was on the news. “Ladies and gentlemen!” the newscaster said. “I’ve never seen this in my life. That baby has to have the biggest, stinkiest diaper I’ve ever seen in my whole life.” Venie’s jaw dropped open. Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie’s diaper wasn’t just big. It wasn’t just huge. It wasn’t just humongous. It was gi-gi-gi-gi-normous! And he was crawling on top of a skyscraper.

Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie didn’t understand what all the fuss was about. There were police officers down below and fire trucks and news cameras. Helicopters circled above him. Sure, his diaper was big, so big the weight of it almost threatened to make the building fall down. But it wasn’t that big of a deal. He only wanted to reach the bird. “Just stay where you are!” the police officers yelled below. “Don’t worry, we’re going to rescue you.” “Ga-ga?” Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie said. “Stinky Binkie!” a voice said. “It’s me, the President of the United States! Don’t worry. We have this situation under control!” Indeed it was him, the President of the United States.

By the time Venie got there, there were a thousand billion people at the building watching Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie. “Stinky Binkie! Stay where you are!” she yelled. “Gaga?” Stinky Binkie said. He was so high up, he could have fallen any moment. His diaper was so gi-gi-gi-normous, the building was starting to shake and quake. “Gaga!” Stinky Binkie said. “Stinky, don’t move!” Venie said. But it was too late. The weight of the diaper was just too much. He started to sway and fray, fray and sway until… “Gaga!” he said and down he went. “Oh, no!” Venie said. He landed diaper first. It cushioned the fall but the entire diaper exploded into a million billion quadrillion pieces. All the goosh and moosh sprayed all over the building, all over the police officers, all over the firemen, all over Venie and even all over the President of the United States. “Ew!” everyone said.

It must have taken Venie four hundred million hours to clean Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie. “You sure did cause a lot of trouble today,” Venie said. She fastened the diaper on him good and tight. Fresh and powdered, he looked at her and said, “Ga-ga?” “Yeah, right.” She frowned but then she smiled. He didn’t look all that bad, after all. In fact, he was kind of cute now that he didn’t stink. She gave him a hug and a kiss. “I love you, Stinky Binkie,” she said. “Ga-ga, goo-goo,” Stinky Binkie replied.

That’s when their mother walked up the stairs, rubbing her eyes and yawning from her nap. “Oh, my goodness. I needed that nap. Well, I see you finally changed his diaper.” “Yep,” Venie said. “Anything exciting happen while I was gone?” her mother asked. Venie blushed and rocked back and forth. “Oh, nothing!” “Goo-goo, ga-ga,” Stinky Binkie Baby Stevie replied. “Sssh,” Venie told him.
THE END
